To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the repatriation process has been successful in empowering Tiwi people to take ownership of the recordings and that the recordings themselves have been empowered as a result of the process.

the repatriation of the recordings was an empowering process that has had a positive effect on Tiwi people’s understanding of their cultural heritage and on the maintenance of Tiwi song tradition, and that the repatriated recordings themselves have become a new source of song material that is being used in contemporary Tiwi song-making.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ways in which the repatriation of song recordings has empowered the Tiwi community, both in its role as a stakeholder in the repatriation process and in its role as the custodian of a body of song material that has been returned to the Tiwi people.

this experience has empowered the Tiwi owners of the recordings and has given them an enhanced appreciation of the value of their cultural heritage.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it has resulted in the empowerment of the Tiwi people and the recordings.
it has been a process of reclaiming, not just the recordings, but the very essence of song as artefact.
we have reclaimed our songs, our culture and our identity, and in doing so we have empowered ourselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Indigenous stakeholders can and should be actively involved in the process of reclaiming their own cultural material, as well as being empowered to use the material in a way that is meaningful to them.
the process of repatriation is not just about returning recordings to the community of origin.
song recordings are not merely artefacts, but are living entities with the power to transform lives and to affect social change.
